say: A tolerance is the honest allowed range. She allows plus or minus 5 grams per ingredient, but only plus or minus 2 grams for salt, because salt affects taste most. The salty-pack complaints stopped.

panel.rule: Every number needs a tolerance: tighter where taste or safety depend.

say: Write six sections. Identity: the product name, size, spec number, version and date. Then each material, its grade and approved supplier.
The formula, with a tolerance beside every quantity. And the process steps in order, with time, heat or mixing conditions.
Describe the finished product: appearance, smell, taste, texture and weight. Then packaging, label version and batch code.
Keep a sealed reference sample from a good batch, and compare against it, not your memory. And write the recipe you really make today.
For food, build the WHO Five Keys to Safer Food into your process steps. Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep food at safe temperatures, and use safe water and raw materials.

panel.heading: Food safety belongs in the spec

cards.d: Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, safe temperatures, safe water and raw materials.
For groundnut products, reject nuts that look mouldy, shrivelled or discoloured.
Declare allergens like groundnut, wheat, milk, egg or soy. Check with NAFDAC before changing a registered product.

say: For groundnut products, reject any nuts that look mouldy, shrivelled or discoloured.

say: Known allergens, such as groundnut, wheat, milk, egg or soy, must be declared. If your product is registered with NAFDAC, check with NAFDAC before changing its formula, pack size or label.

say: Products drift through small unrecorded changes. Change control stops that. For example, Hauwa's new pepper supplier sells hotter pepper. She writes a proposal.
She makes two trial batches the same day: the old pepper at 200 grams, and the new at 170 grams, with groundnut powder raised to 630.
10 regular customers taste both, unlabelled. 7 cannot tell the difference or prefer the new one.
The label order stays the same, so she records version 1.1 in her change log.
Then she shows her packer the new weights. Change one thing at a time, and keep a sealed sample of the old version.
Now weigh your real recipe three times and write your one-page spec, version 1.0. Complete your readiness scorecard with a second person. Then start your change log.
